To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PC3 prostate cancer cells contain three different cell variants that differ in morphology and integrin expression; 2) TPA increases the invasiveness and the expression of beta1 integrins; 3) PC3 variants differ also in MMP9 and PAI-1 activities.
PC3 prostate cancer cells show phenotypic heterogeniety in culture conditions.
the PC3 prostate cancer variant cell lines are heterogeneous, and that the culture condition modulates cell phenotype and selects subpopulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in prostate cancer progression.
the identification of molecular markers of tumor aggressiveness and with the definition of the role of the cell adhesion in the modulation of tumor phenotype.
the study of the role of integrins in the control of tumor invasion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell phenotype and cell function are modulated by culture conditions.
cell variants are selected by the culture condition and that this may represent a good tool to study tumor progression in vitro.
the PC3 cell line represents a good model to study tumor cell heterogeneity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell culture environment may influence cell phenotype, causing selection of subpopulated variants.
the PC3 prostate cancer line contains three variants, which differ in cell morphology, cell spreading, integrin expression, MMP9, uPA and TIMP1 secretion.
PC3 cell line, cultured under specific conditions, may represent a model for tumor heterogeneity and progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PC3 cell line is a good model to study the role of the extracellular matrix and integrins in tumor progression and metastasis.
PC3 is not a homogeneous cell line and that different culture conditions can select subpopulations with different phenotypes.
the cell line PC3, when grown in culture, shows different phenotypic variants that can be selected by the culture conditions and that may be useful for the study of tumor heterogeneity.
